Impressing for her county all season and in The Hundred, which she won with Trent Rockets, Luff was also selected in the Metro Bank PCA Women's Team of the Year.

"It's super special people have voted for me after the performances and impact they feel I've had this year. It means that I'm doing things in the right way, and people think highly of you," said the 32-year-old, who scored more than 1,000 runs this summer.

"I've always been a leader that wants to lead from the front, but I think people are seeing that play out in games now. I think this year I've just showcased what I'm capable of."

articles.title: AL Wild Card Series Game 2: Max Fried vs. Sonny Gray
articles.summary: A win tonight sends the Yankees to the ALDS.
articles.body:
In the words of a Yankee legend, it was dèja vu all over again in the Bronx last night as Cam Schlittler continued crafting a legend of his own. Just like last season, Schlittler delivered a gem of a performance against the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, staking New York to a 1-0 series lead and giving them an opportunity to close the affair out early tonight. But unlike last year's three-game set, in which the Yankee offense never fully erupted, the lineup finally achieved escape velocity. Ben Rice and his four hits, two homers, and six RBI, led the charge — but the bottom of the lineup contributed their fair share as well.

In other words, the Yankees played the perfect ballgame last night. Max Fried will be tasked with carrying the momentum into Game 2. Fried's second season in pinstripes has been marred by a couple of IL stints limiting him to just 20 starts and 112.2 innings, but when he's been healthy, he's been just as good as in 2025. He'll be pitching on seven days' rest in Game 2 — his last appearance was an up-and-down start against the Rays , in which Tampa clinched the AL East.

As far as the recent track record against Boston, Fried has been quite effective. He only faced them twice this season: one was a short start from when he was returning from his latest injury, the other an eight-inning masterpiece in April from before the Red Sox got it together under new manager Chad Tracy. In Game 1 of last year's WCS, he provided 6.1 scoreless innings, scattering four hits three walks while striking out six. The Yankees couldn't hold onto the narrow 1-0 lead he had defended, and sabotaged their own comeback effort after loading the bases with nobody out in the ninth inning. None of that was Max's fault, of course. Provided the lineup supports him, an effort like last year's will be more than enough.

Old friend Sonny Gray never caught on with the Yankees in 2017 and 2018, but he'll have no choice but to step up under the Yankee Stadium lights with Boston's season on the line. Over his first season with the Red Sox, the steady veteran turned in yet another outstanding season, leading the AL with 18 wins (don't think that doesn't mean anything to him) and pitching to a 2.72 ERA. That's the thing about the Red Sox' pitching: they have lots of exciting youngsters like Payton Tolle , who pitched last night, but they also routinely get the most out of their veteran pitchers too. Gray faced New York twice in June and pitched well both times. The latter outing was his best start of the season by game score — one hit, one walk, nine strikeouts over 7.1 scoreless innings.

Unsurprisingly, Aaron Boone's lineup for Game 2 is nearly unrecognizable when compared with the Game 1 starting nine. It's a history-making card: according to James Smyth of the YES Network , it's the first time a team has put eight lefty batters — switch hitters not included — in the same lineup in the postseason. The portside octet includes Trent Grisham , who entered late last night for his first action off the IL. Rice will ascend to the leadoff spot, with Cody Bellinger and Luis Garcia Jr. to follow. Spencer Jones hits cleanup and plays right field ahead of George Lombard Jr., the lone righty to get the start. Jazz Chisholm Jr. draws in at the keystone, Grisham bats in the seven-spot after him, Austin Wells will bat eighth, and Ryan McMahon starts at third and will hit ninth. Naturally, expect plenty of right-handed bats to come off the bench against a lefty-heavy Boston staff once Gray's start concludes.

articles.title: Shubman Gill smashes fastest ODI double century as India chase down West Indies’ 406 with 39 balls to spare
articles.summary: GUWAHATI: Shubman Gill produced a breathtaking batting masterclass to smash the fastest double century in ODI cricket history as India chased down West
articles.body: GUWAHATI: Shubman Gill produced a breathtaking batting masterclass to smash the fastest double century in ODI cricket history as India chased down West Indies’ imposing 406-run target with 39 balls to spare in the second ODI at Barsapara Cricket Stadium here on Wednesday. The eight-wicket win, second on the trot, also sealed the three-match series in the hosts’ favour.Gill remained unbeaten on 223 (133 balls, 28x4, 8x6) eclipsing Ishan Kishan’s previous mark of a 126-ball double century against Bangladesh. It was Gill’s second ODI double ton, after his 208 against New Zealand in Hyderabad in 2023, leaving him behind only Rohit Sharma, who has three, on the list of Indian batters with multiple double centuries.Reaching 200-run mark (117 balls), Gill had earlier raced to his 11th ODI century in just 62 balls, setting the tone for an extraordinary assault. He continued to find boundaries at will, combining precise cuts and drives with powerful strokes all around the park as India kept the pressure firmly on the West Indies attack.At the other end, Rohit Sharma provided the perfect launchpad with a 101 off 75 balls. The opener completed his 35th ODI century and, in the process, crossed 12,000 runs in the format, becoming only the third Indian after Sachin Tendulkar and Virat Kohli and the seventh batter overall to reach the milestone.Rohit was dismissed immediately after reaching three figures, trapped lbw by Jayden Seales. He had earlier been given a reprieve on 84 when Keacy Carty dropped him at deep mid-wicket. Gill and Rohit’s opening stand of 255 runs fell just three runs short of Sachin Tendulkar and Sourav Ganguly’s all-time record of 258 runs scored against Kenya in 2001.Virat Kohli made 29 before falling while attempting to guide a bouncer. Gill, however, remained in complete command. His unbeaten knock carried India to 406/2 and their highest successful ODI chase, surpassing their previous best of 362/1 against Australia in Jaipur in 2013. The victory was also the highest successful chase on Indian soil and the second-highest successful chase in ODI cricket. South Africa’s 438/9 against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006 remains the benchmark.India’s remarkable pursuit followed an extraordinary batting display from Windies, who posted 405/7 — their highest ODI total against India. For the first time in their ODI history, three West Indies batters scored centuries in the same innings. John Campbell struck 101 off 68 balls (9x4, 5x6), captain Shai Hope made 104 off 94 (8x4, 3x6), while Amir Jangoo top-scored with a 114 off 77 (13x3, 3x6)Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘This is not cricket’: Gautam Gambhir questions Guwahati pitch after India chase 406 with ease
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had little doubt about the entertainment value of Wednesday’s extraordinary run-fest in Guwahati, but he was
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India head coach Gautam Gambhir had little doubt about the entertainment value of Wednesday’s extraordinary run-fest in Guwahati, but he was far less impressed by the conditions that allowed both teams to score more than 400 runs.After West Indies posted 405 for seven, India chased down the target in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets to seal the three-match ODI series 2-0. Shubman Gill smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls, while Rohit Sharma scored 101 off 75 as India completed the highest successful run chase in their ODI history.Yet, for Gambhir, the remarkable numbers also highlighted a concern. He felt the pitch offered too little to the bowlers and called for a greater balance between bat and ball.“Look, if I have to be absolutely honest, I feel I think there has to be a bit of more contest between bat and ball, because I think you talk about cricket - but this is not cricket, this is only batting,” Gambhir told Star Sports after the match.“Because imagine a young bowler bowling on this wicket, and the opposition getting 400 and then we go on to chase 400. Obviously, for the records it's outstanding, for the crowd it's outstanding, for the broadcaster it's outstanding, but if you ask me as a genuine cricket fan and as a coach, because I have to have sympathy for the bowlers as well.”“When you bowl on this kind of a wicket, it's not fair for the bowlers. So we've got to give something to the bowlers so there's at least something which the bowlers can work with,” he added.‘It’s not fair for the bowlers’The Guwahati surface produced a stunning batting display, with West Indies reaching 405 for seven before India responded with 406 for two.John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo struck centuries for West Indies, while Gill and Rohit then led the Indian chase. Gill's unbeaten 223 was the defining innings of the day, while his opening partnership of 255 with Rohit was India's second-highest in men's ODIs.Virat Kohli, who had scored a century in the first ODI, contributed 29 off 19 balls before falling, while Ruturaj Gaikwad made 31 off 37.The match became only the second successful chase of a target of 400 or more in men's ODI history, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in 2006.For Gambhir, however, the scale of the scoring made it important to consider what the conditions meant for the bowlers rather than simply celebrating the batting numbers.“The first thing is that you need some sympathy and a bit of margin for the bowlers,” he said.“Often you can't be hard on bowlers, because sometimes bowling figures are such that they haven't bowled as poorly as their figures suggest. Because the margin is very small.”He also pointed to the restrictions modern-day bowlers face in ODI cricket, including fielding restrictions, two new balls and the increasing power of batters.“Plus, I think you can only bowl in good areas because besides that, with five fielders inside, two new balls, and the kind of power-hitting there is now, bowlers don't really have many options,” Gambhir said.“That is why, as a coach, as a support staff, the first thing you look at is, were they able to execute their bowling or their plans properly? If they were able to do that, then you shouldn't be hard on them.”“If you get too hard just looking at their analysis, then we will never be able to develop bowlers.”Gambhir backs exposure for young bowlersIndia gave Auqib Nabi his ODI debut despite already leading the series 1-0, and Gambhir said putting inexperienced bowlers into difficult situations was an important part of India's preparation for the 2027 ODI World Cup.“Imagine Auqib [Nabi] playing his first game... somewhere you need to give them a bit of support and keep a bit of an extra cushion or extra options for them,” he said. “But unfortunately, today there wasn't much for any bowler.”Gambhir said India could have waited until the third ODI, when the series would already be decided, to give Nabi an opportunity. But he argued that a dead rubber would not recreate the pressure young players could experience at a World Cup.“We could have given Auqib a chance in the next match too when it's a dead rubber, but in a dead rubber, you don't have that pressure which comes with the pressure of winning a series,” he said.“And we all know that the World Cup is all about pressure. Cricket isn't going to change like that, only the pressure will be different because the World Cup comes once in four years, so we want to put bowlers under pressure.”He also cited Gurnoor Brar as an example of a young bowler who could benefit from being exposed to demanding phases of an ODI.“For example, Gurnoor [Brar]. Having Gurnoor bowl in the first 10 overs, bowling at the death, I know people will talk about his analysis, but the more he bowls in tough conditions, in tough situations, the better it is for Indian cricket,” Gambhir said.“Because you can have him bowl in the middle overs and get good analysis or good stats for him, make him bowl defensively, but the more we expose them at such times, the better it is for Indian cricket.”Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill scripts history, becomes first captain to score double centuries in Test and ODIs
articles.summary: Shubman Gill did not just produce another breathtaking innings on Wednesday night.
articles.body: Shubman Gill did not just produce another breathtaking innings on Wednesday night. He created a record that had never been achieved in international cricket before.The Indian captain smashed an unbeaten 223 off 133 balls against West Indies in the second ODI in Guwahati, becoming the first captain to score a double century in both Test and ODI cricket. Gill had previously scored 269 against England at Edgbaston in 2025, making his latest feat a unique chapter in the history of captaincy.What made the Guwahati innings even more remarkable was the situation. West Indies had posted 405/7, their first-ever 400-plus ODI total, after centuries from John Campbell, Shai Hope and Amir Jangoo. India then chased down 406 in just 43.3 overs, winning by eight wickets with 39 balls to spare.From Edgbaston 269 to Guwahati 223*Gill's latest record cannot be viewed in isolation. In July 2025, while leading India in the Test series against England, he produced historic innings at Edgbaston. His 269 off 387 balls became the highest score by an Indian captain in Test cricket and the highest score by an Indian captain in a Test in England.That innings already placed Gill in an exclusive group of captains to score Test double centuries in England. Now, with his Guwahati double century, he has added an unprecedented ODI achievement to that record. Gill became the first captain to score a double century in both Test and ODI cricket.Fastest double century in ODI historyGill reached his double century in just 117 balls, breaking Ishan Kishan's previous record of 126 balls. His 223* also became the highest individual score in a successful ODI chase, surpassing Glenn Maxwell's unbeaten 201 against Afghanistan.By the time he reached 223, Gill had hit 26 fours and eight sixes, finishing with the highest ODI score of his career. His previous best was the 208 he scored against New Zealand in Hyderabad in 2023.That makes Gill only the second Indian after Rohit Sharma to score multiple ODI double centuries. Rohit remains the only batter with three ODI double tons.Gill's individual brilliance came during a chase that itself entered the record books. India's 406/2 became their highest successful ODI chase, surpassing their previous record. It was also only the second time a team had successfully chased a target of 400 or more in men's ODI cricket, after South Africa's famous 438-run chase against Australia in Johannesburg in 2006.The foundation was laid by Gill and Rohit Sharma, who put together a remarkable 255-run opening partnership. Rohit contributed 101 before being dismissed, leaving Gill to complete the chase alongside Ruturaj Gaikwad.The match therefore produced an unusual statistical symmetry: West Indies made 405, three of their batters scored centuries, and India chased the target with two centuries of their own.The Guwahati double century also took Gill to his 11th ODI century in just 68 innings. He became the fastest Indian to reach 11 ODI hundreds, moving ahead of Virat Kohli's mark of 82 innings. Hashim Amla remains the fastest overall, having reached the milestone in 64 innings.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.summary: Pakistan star Babar Azam was involved in an unusual incident during a President’s Trophy Grade-I match in Islamabad on Wednesday, September 30, after
articles.body: Pakistan star Babar Azam was involved in an unusual incident during a President’s Trophy Grade-I match in Islamabad on Wednesday, September 30, after multiple spectators breached security and entered the playing area to get selfies with him.A video doing the rounds on social media shows Babar fielding for Oil and Gas Development Company Limited (OGDCL) against State Bank of Pakistan (SBP) at the Diamond Cricket Ground when fans approached him with their phones. Babar appeared to push one fan away and gesture for him to leave the field. When another spectator approached him for a selfie, the Pakistan batter took the fan’s phone and threw it away before asking the spectators to leave.The incident highlighted security concerns at the venue, with reports suggesting fans had entered the field multiple times during Babar’s return to domestic cricket. The situation escalated further after Babar was dismissed for 21 off 39 balls. Several spectators rushed onto the field and surrounded him as he walked back to the pavilion, forcing ground staff to intervene and escort him away from the crowd.Following the incidents, Islamabad Police increased security arrangements at the ground to control the gathering and prevent further breaches. articles.title: Irani Cup returns to Srinagar's Sher-i-Kashmir Stadium amid heightened security
articles.summary: SRINAGAR: Giant billboards greet visitors entering the Jammu & Kashmir Cricket Association premises in Srinagar’s high-security Church Lane.
articles.body: SRINAGAR: Giant billboards greet visitors entering the Jammu & Kashmir Cricket Association premises in Srinagar’s high-security Church Lane.One features local cricketer Auqib Nabi, highlighting his Ranji performance and describing him as India’s No.1 fast bowler. Another celebrates the Jammu and Kashmir team as Ranji champions.The Sher-i-Kashmir stadium opens into a setting of towering chinar trees, with the Zabarwan mountain range visible ahead.Many describe it the country’s most beautiful cricket ground. Preparations for the Irani Cup, scheduled to start here from Thursday, are being given final touches. In the 5,000-capacity stadium invitations for the matches have been sent to a select audience, officials said, citing the stadium’s past history. “We don’t want to take any chances,” an official said. Only one gate would be used as the main entry point, while the others would remain closed.On Oct 13, 1983, during the first international cricket match here between India and the visiting West Indies, the Indian team — having won the World Cup only a few months before — faced an unexpected reaction from the crowd. The newly crowned world champion team was booed by sections of the crowd, while the West Indies cricketers — who won the game — unexpectedly felt at home in the Valley. Former captain Sunil Gavaskar later wrote in ‘Runs ’n’ Ruins’ that being hooted at after a defeat is understandable, but this was incredible. He also said there were many in the crowd shouting pro-Pakistan slogans which confounded them as they were playing the West Indies, and not Pakistan.A similar controversy erupted in Sept 1986 during a match between Australia and India at the same venue. Some youths dug up the pitch, prompting police to register an FIR during the initial stages of the game. The accused were later arrested on charges of damaging the pitch. Against this backdrop, the Irani Cup will headline a series of major cricket events at the venue, with three competitions being held back to back. “It is a big trophy for Jammu and Kashmir (to try to win),” a JKCA official said.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: How to watch 2027 ODI World Cup schedule announcement live: TV channel, live stream details
articles.summary: With the ICC finally releasing the groups and schedule for the 2027 ODI World Cup, here's where you can watch the livestream worldwide.
articles.body:
The ICC will unveil the 2027 World Cup schedule and groups at an event in Cape Town, South Africa , on October 1.

The launch show begins at 5:30 p.m. SAST (9:00 p.m. IST) and will stream free on the ICC's YouTube channel.

The ticket ballot for the tournament also opens on the same day and runs until November 21, 2026.

The 2027 World Cup draw is finally here, and the coverage is global

The countdown to the 2027 Men's Cricket World Cup reaches a major milestone on Thursday, with the ICC confirming the schedule launch show will air live from the Zeitz Museum of Contemporary Art Africa in Cape Town. The event doubles as the opening of the tournament's ticket ballot.

Fourteen teams will contest 57 matches across 12 venues in South Africa, Zimbabwe and Namibia, and Thursday's broadcast is expected to confirm both the groups and the full fixture list a year ahead of the opening match.

The ICC has published a detailed broadcast list covering every major cricketing market, so fans know exactly where to tune in regardless of their region.

Where to watch the schedule launch in India

TV channel: Star Sports 1, Star Sports 1 Hindi, Star Sports 2, Star Sports 2 Hindi, Star Sports 3 Live streaming: JioHotstar

JioStar holds the rights in India, with the launch show carried live across the Star Sports network and streamed on JioHotstar.

Where to watch the schedule launch in Sri Lanka

TV channel: DTV Live streaming: Dialog Play App

Dialog will broadcast the event live in Sri Lanka, with coverage available on DTV and through the Dialog Play App.

Where to watch the schedule launch in South Africa

TV channel: SuperSport Cricket, SuperSport Cricket Africa, SuperSport Grandstand, SuperSport Grandstand Africa Live streaming: SuperSport Africa ROA, SuperSport Africa SA

SuperSport carries the launch show across South Africa and the wider Sub-Saharan Africa region, with multiple channels within its network airing the broadcast.

Where to watch the schedule launch in Australia

TV channel: Not available Live streaming: Amazon Prime Video (on-demand)

Unlike most other territories, the launch show will not be available live in Australia. Prime Video will instead carry the event on demand after it airs.

Where to watch the schedule launch in the UK

TV channel: Sky Sports Cricket Live streaming: Sky Sports app

Sky Sports holds the rights in the UK, with the launch show airing live on Sky Sports Cricket.

Where to watch the schedule launch in the USA and Canada

TV channel: Willow TV Live streaming: Willow TV app

Fans across the United States and Canada can follow the launch live through Willow TV.

Where to watch the schedule launch in New Zealand

TV channel: Not confirmed at this time Live streaming: ICC YouTube

The ICC has not listed any dedicated New Zealand broadcaster. Fans in the country can still follow the event through the ICC's free global YouTube stream.

Where to watch the schedule launch in Pakistan

TV channel: PTV, Geo Super Live streaming: Myco, Tamasha

Pakistani fans have multiple options, with PTV and Geo Super carrying the broadcast on television, and Myco and Tamasha offering digital streams.

Where to watch the schedule launch in Bangladesh

Bangladesh does not appear on the ICC's official broadcaster list for this event. Fans can instead rely on the free global stream via ICC's YouTube channel.

Where to watch the schedule launch in the Caribbean

TV channel: ESPN Caribbean Live streaming: Disney+

ESPN holds the rights across the Caribbean, with the launch show airing live on ESPN Caribbean and also available through Disney+.

Where to watch the schedule launch in the UAE

TV channel: Not available Live streaming: StarzPlay Cricket

The UAE is covered under the ICC's wider Middle East and North Africa rights deal with Etisalat, with StarzPlay Cricket the only listed way to stream the launch show live in the region.

ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 schedule launch: Broadcast details worldwide

ICC Men's Cricket World Cup 2027 schedule launch: Start time worldwide

The broadcast is set to go live at 5:30 PM local time, with simultaneous coverage across every major cricketing nation. The ICC's official YouTube channel will also show the draw live, alongside TV and streaming options.
